subproblem.title: Lower left closed-band density of ν is at most the lower left Dini derivative of its distribution function on (a,b) (parent Step 4 / (5a))
subproblem.statement: Let ν be a Borel measure on ℝ and a, b ∈ ℝ with ν((a,b)) < ∞. Let G(r) := ν((a,b) ∩ (−∞, r]), taken as a real number (toReal). Then for every t ∈ (a,b), liminf_{h→0+} ν([t − h, t])/ofReal(h) ≤ liminf_{k→0+} ofReal((G(t) − G(t − k))/k). Both liminfs are taken in [0, ∞] along 𝓝[>] 0, and the quotient on the left is division in [0, ∞].
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (ν : Measure ℝ) (a b : ℝ), ν (Ioo a b) ≠ ∞ → ∀ t ∈ Ioo a b, liminf (fun h : ℝ => ν (Icc (t - h) t) / ENNReal.ofReal h) (𝓝[>] 0) ≤ liminf (fun k : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal (((ν (Ioo a b ∩ Iic t)).toReal - (ν (Ioo a b ∩ Iic (t - k))).toReal) / k)) (𝓝[>] 0)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, Step 4 ((5a): Λ(t) ≤ D(t)), parts (a)–(d), together with Step 2(a),(b) (monotonicity and increments of G). Here it is stated for an arbitrary Borel measure ν with ν((a,b)) < ∞. In the parent, the right-hand side is D(t) and the claim is Λ(t) ≤ D(t).

Setting. Fix t ∈ (a,b). For r ∈ ℝ let A_r := (a,b) ∩ (−∞, r] and G(r) := (ν(A_r)).toReal. For h ∈ ℝ put φ(h) := ν([t − h, t])/ofReal(h) and Λ := liminf_{h→0+} φ(h). For k ∈ ℝ put F(k) := ofReal((G(t) − G(t − k))/k) and D := liminf_{k→0+} F(k). Both liminfs are along 𝓝[>] 0 in [0, ∞].

1. (Finiteness and monotonicity; Step 2(a).) For every r, A_r ⊆ (a,b), so ν(A_r) ≤ ν((a,b)) < ∞. If r ≤ r′, then A_r ⊆ A_{r′}, so ν(A_r) ≤ ν(A_{r′}). Both values are finite, so G(r) ≤ G(r′) (`ENNReal.toReal_mono`). Thus G is nondecreasing.

2. (Increments; Step 2(b).) Let s′ ≤ s and B := (a,b) ∩ (s′, s].
 (i) Every x ∈ A_s satisfies either x ≤ s′ (so x ∈ A_{s′}) or s′ < x ≤ s (so x ∈ B). Conversely, A_{s′} ⊆ A_s because s′ ≤ s, and B ⊆ A_s. Hence A_s = A_{s′} ∪ B.
 (ii) The union is disjoint (x ≤ s′ and s′ < x are incompatible), and B is Borel.
 (iii) By additivity (`measure_union`), ν(A_s) = ν(A_{s′}) + ν(B).
 (iv) All three values are finite, since they are ≤ ν((a,b)). Taking real parts (`ENNReal.toReal_add`) gives G(s) = G(s′) + (ν(B)).toReal, i.e. (ν(B)).toReal = G(s) − G(s′).
 (v) Therefore ν((a,b) ∩ (s′, s]) = ofReal(G(s) − G(s′)) (`ENNReal.ofReal_toReal`).

3. (Band comparison; Step 4(a).) Fix a real c > 1. Let k ∈ (0, t − a), which is nonempty because t > a, and put h := k/c.
 (i) 0 < h < k because c > 1, hence a < t − k < t − h. Also t < b. So every x ∈ [t − h, t] satisfies a < t − k < t − h ≤ x ≤ t < b, i.e. [t − h, t] ⊆ (a,b) ∩ (t − k, t].
 (ii) By monotonicity of ν and step 2 (with s′ = t − k ≤ s = t): ν([t − h, t]) ≤ ν((a,b) ∩ (t − k, t]) = ofReal(G(t) − G(t − k)).
 (iii) Put Δ := (G(t) − G(t − k))/k. By step 1, G(t − k) ≤ G(t), so Δ ≥ 0. Since k = c·h, G(t) − G(t − k) = k·Δ = c·Δ·h.
 (iv) As c ≥ 0 and c·Δ ≥ 0, ofReal is multiplicative here (`ENNReal.ofReal_mul`, applied twice): ofReal(c·Δ·h) = ofReal(c)·ofReal(Δ)·ofReal(h). Hence ν([t − h, t]) ≤ ofReal(c)·F(k)·ofReal(h).
 (v) Dividing by ofReal(h) (`ENNReal.div_le_of_le_mul`) gives φ(k/c) ≤ ofReal(c)·F(k) for every k ∈ (0, t − a).
 Since (0, t − a) ∈ 𝓝[>] 0 (`Ioo_mem_nhdsGT`), this inequality holds eventually along 𝓝[>] 0.

4. (Reparametrization; Step 4(b).) The map k ↦ k/c is continuous, sends 0 to 0/c = 0, and maps (0, ∞) into (0, ∞) because c > 0. So it tends from 𝓝[>] 0 to 𝓝[>] 0 (`tendsto_nhdsWithin_of_tendsto_nhds_of_eventually_within`). Composing a function with a map that tends to the filter can only increase the liminf (`Filter.Tendsto.liminf_le_liminf_comp`; in the complete lattice [0, ∞] all boundedness side conditions hold). So Λ = liminf_{h→0+} φ(h) ≤ liminf_{k→0+} φ(k/c).

5. (Constant factor; Step 4(c).) By step 3 and `Filter.liminf_le_liminf`, liminf_{k→0+} φ(k/c) ≤ liminf_{k→0+} ofReal(c)·F(k). Since ofReal(c) ≠ ∞ and 𝓝[>] 0 is a nontrivial filter, the constant factors out (`ENNReal.liminf_const_mul_of_ne_top`): liminf_{k→0+} ofReal(c)·F(k) = ofReal(c)·D. Together with step 4: Λ ≤ ofReal(c)·D for every c > 1.

6. (Letting c ↓ 1; Step 4(d).) If D = ∞, then Λ ≤ D trivially. Otherwise let c_n := 1 + 1/(n+1) > 1. Then c_n → 1, so ofReal(c_n) → ofReal(1) = 1 (`ENNReal.tendsto_ofReal`). Since D ≠ ∞, ofReal(c_n)·D → 1·D = D (`ENNReal.Tendsto.mul_const`). By step 5, Λ ≤ ofReal(c_n)·D for every n, so Λ ≤ D (`ge_of_tendsto`).

7. (Conclusion.) Λ ≤ D, i.e. liminf_{h→0+} ν([t − h, t])/ofReal(h) ≤ liminf_{k→0+} ofReal((G(t) − G(t − k))/k). This is the parent's comparison of the closed band [t − h, t] with the slightly wider half-open band (t − k, t], first at a fixed width ratio k/h = c and then as c ↓ 1. ∎
proof_key_steps: G(r) = ν((a,b) ∩ (−∞,r]).toReal is finite and nondecreasing. For s′ ≤ s, disjoint additivity gives ν((a,b) ∩ (s′, s]) = ofReal(G(s) − G(s′)).
For c > 1, 0 < k < t − a and h = k/c: [t−h, t] ⊆ (a,b) ∩ (t−k, t], so φ(k/c) = ν([t−h,t])/ofReal(h) ≤ ofReal(c)·ofReal((G(t) − G(t−k))/k).
k ↦ k/c maps 𝓝[>] 0 to 𝓝[>] 0, so Λ ≤ liminf φ(k/c) ≤ liminf ofReal(c)·F(k) = ofReal(c)·D (Tendsto.liminf_le_liminf_comp, liminf_le_liminf, ENNReal.liminf_const_mul_of_ne_top).
With c_n = 1 + 1/(n+1) ↓ 1, ofReal(c_n)·D → D when D < ∞, so Λ ≤ D.

audit.reason: Finite disjoint increments justify the real-valued distribution formula. The strict c-dilation gives the required closed-band inclusion, positive-denominator division, and correctly directed liminf comparison. Constant extraction and c ↓ 1 handle both finite and infinite D. All hypotheses are accounted for, with no sibling dependency or circular step.

subproblem.title: Integral over (a,b) of the lower left Dini derivative of a nondecreasing function is at most G(b) − G(a) (parent Step 7 / (5d), Lebesgue's theorem)
subproblem.statement: Let G : ℝ → ℝ be nondecreasing and let a ≤ b. Let D(t) := liminf_{k→0+} ofReal((G(t) − G(t − k))/k) ∈ [0, ∞], with the liminf along 𝓝[>] 0 in [0, ∞]. Then ∫⁻_{(a,b)} D(t) dt ≤ ofReal(G(b) − G(a)), where ∫⁻ is the lower Lebesgue integral with respect to Lebesgue measure dt.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ G : ℝ → ℝ, Monotone G → ∀ a b : ℝ, a ≤ b → ∫⁻ t in Ioo a b, liminf (fun k : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal ((G t - G (t - k)) / k)) (𝓝[>] 0) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (G b - G a)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, Step 7 ((5d): integral bound via Lebesgue's theorem). Here it is stated for an arbitrary nondecreasing G : ℝ → ℝ and a ≤ b. The parent applies it to its distribution function G with its a < b, where G(a) = 0 and G(b) = ν((a,b)) by its Step 2(c). Simon's printed argument for Ch. 6, 4.10 is exactly this: an increasing function is differentiable L¹-a.e., and the integral of its derivative over [a,b] is at most its increment.

Implementation note: `MonotoneOn.intervalIntegrable_deriv` and `MonotoneOn.intervalIntegral_deriv_mem_uIcc` are in `Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.IntervalIntegral.DerivIntegrable`. That module is not in the import closure of the frozen Submission header, so `import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.IntervalIntegral.DerivIntegrable` must be added to GMT/Ch06/Submission.lean. The comparator byte-checks only the frozen contract and the build inputs, and accepted Ch06 children have added imports. `Monotone.ae_differentiableAt` is already in the frozen closure.

Setting. λ is Lebesgue measure on ℝ. G′ := deriv G is the derivative where G is differentiable and 0 elsewhere. D(t) := liminf_{k→0+} ofReal((G(t) − G(t − k))/k).

1. (Lebesgue's theorem; Step 7(a).) G is monotone, so G is differentiable at λ-a.e. s ∈ ℝ (`Monotone.ae_differentiableAt`).

2. (D = ofReal(G′) at points of differentiability; Step 7(b).) Let G be differentiable at s, so G has derivative G′(s) at s.
 (i) The slope (G(y) − G(s))/(y − s) tends to G′(s) as y → s with y ≠ s (`HasDerivAt.tendsto_slope`, filter 𝓝[≠] s).
 (ii) The map k ↦ s − k is continuous, takes the value s at k = 0, and satisfies s − k ≠ s for k > 0. So it maps the filter 𝓝[>] 0 into 𝓝[≠] s.
 (iii) For k > 0 the slope at y = s − k is (G(s − k) − G(s))/((s − k) − s) = (G(s − k) − G(s))/(−k) = (G(s) − G(s − k))/k (`slope_def_field`).
 (iv) Hence (G(s) − G(s − k))/k → G′(s) as k → 0+. By continuity of ofReal, ofReal((G(s) − G(s − k))/k) → ofReal(G′(s)) along 𝓝[>] 0.
 (v) The filter 𝓝[>] 0 on ℝ is nontrivial, and in [0, ∞] the liminf of a convergent function is its limit (`Filter.Tendsto.liminf_eq`). Thus D(s) = ofReal(G′(s)).
 By step 1, D = ofReal ∘ G′ λ-a.e. on ℝ, hence also a.e. for λ restricted to (a,b) (`ae_restrict_of_ae`).

3. (Properties of G′; Step 7(c).)
 (i) G′(x) ≥ 0 for every x (`Monotone.deriv_nonneg`): where G is differentiable, G′(x) is a limit of nonnegative difference quotients; elsewhere G′(x) = 0.
 (ii) G is monotone on [a,b] = uIcc a b, so G′ is interval integrable on [a,b] (`MonotoneOn.intervalIntegrable_deriv`). As a ≤ b, this means G′ is integrable on (a,b] (`intervalIntegrable_iff_integrableOn_Ioc_of_le`), hence on (a,b) ⊆ (a,b] (`IntegrableOn.mono_set`).
 (iii) ∫_a^b G′ dλ ∈ uIcc 0 (G(b) − G(a)) (`MonotoneOn.intervalIntegral_deriv_mem_uIcc`). Since G(a) ≤ G(b), uIcc 0 (G(b) − G(a)) = [0, G(b) − G(a)], so ∫_a^b G′ dλ ≤ G(b) − G(a).

4. (Integration; Step 7(d).)
 ∫⁻_{(a,b)} D dλ = ∫⁻_{(a,b)} ofReal(G′) dλ, by step 2 and `lintegral_congr_ae`;
 = ofReal(∫_{(a,b)} G′ dλ), by `ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal`, which applies because G′ is integrable on (a,b) and G′ ≥ 0 (step 3(i),(ii));
 = ofReal(∫_a^b G′ dλ), because `intervalIntegral.integral_of_le` gives ∫_a^b G′ = ∫_{(a,b]} G′, and `integral_Ioc_eq_integral_Ioo` gives ∫_{(a,b]} G′ = ∫_{(a,b)} G′ ({b} is λ-null);
 ≤ ofReal(G(b) − G(a)), by step 3(iii) and monotonicity of ofReal (`ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal`).

5. (Conclusion.) ∫⁻_{(a,b)} D(t) dt ≤ ofReal(G(b) − G(a)). No measurability of D is needed: the lower Lebesgue integral is defined for every [0, ∞]-valued function and is invariant under a.e. equality. If a = b, then (a,b) = ∅ and the same chain applies with all integrals equal to 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: At a differentiability point s, (G(s) − G(s−k))/k = slope G s (s−k) → G′(s) as k → 0+. So D(s) = ofReal(G′(s)) (Filter.Tendsto.liminf_eq), and hence D = ofReal ∘ deriv G a.e.

deriv G ≥ 0 everywhere (Monotone.deriv_nonneg). MonotoneOn.intervalIntegrable_deriv and MonotoneOn.intervalIntegral_deriv_mem_uIcc give integrability on (a,b) and ∫_a^b G′ ≤ G(b) − G(a) (needs import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.IntervalIntegral.DerivIntegrable).
∫⁻_{(a,b)} D = ∫⁻_{(a,b)} ofReal(G′) = ofReal(∫_{(a,b)} G′) = ofReal(∫_a^b G′) ≤ ofReal(G(b) − G(a)).

subproblem.title: Lower left Dini derivative of a nondecreasing right-continuous function is Borel (parent Step 5 / (5b))
subproblem.statement: Let G : ℝ → ℝ be nondecreasing and right-continuous at every point: for every s ∈ ℝ, G(r) → G(s) as r → s within [s, ∞). For t ∈ ℝ define the lower left Dini derivative D(t) := liminf_{k→0+} ofReal((G(t) − G(t − k))/k) ∈ [0, ∞]. The liminf is taken in [0, ∞] along the filter 𝓝[>] 0. Then D : ℝ → [0, ∞] is Borel measurable.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ G : ℝ → ℝ, Monotone G → (∀ s : ℝ, ContinuousWithinAt G (Ici s) s) → Measurable (fun t : ℝ => liminf (fun k : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal ((G t - G (t - k)) / k)) (𝓝[>] 0))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, Step 5 ((5b): Borel measurability of D by a rational infimum), parts (a)–(d). Here it is stated for an arbitrary nondecreasing right-continuous G : ℝ → ℝ. The parent applies it to its distribution function G, which is nondecreasing and right-continuous by its Step 2(a),(d) (sibling lemma distribution_regularity). Step 2(e) (a monotone function is Borel) is used in step 5 below.

Setting. G : ℝ → ℝ is nondecreasing, and for every s ∈ ℝ, G(r) → G(s) as r → s within [s, ∞). For t, k ∈ ℝ put F_t(k) := ofReal((G(t) − G(t − k))/k) ∈ [0, ∞). Put D(t) := liminf_{k→0+} F_t(k) ∈ [0, ∞], the liminf in the complete lattice [0, ∞] along the filter 𝓝[>] 0.

1. (A countable basis of 𝓝[>] 0.) The intervals (0, δ), δ > 0, form a basis of 𝓝[>] 0 (`nhdsGT_basis`). For every δ > 0 there is j ∈ ℕ with 1/(j+1) < δ (`exists_nat_one_div_lt`), and then (0, 1/(j+1)) ⊆ (0, δ). Conversely, each (0, 1/(j+1)) is a basic set (0, δ) with δ = 1/(j+1) > 0. Hence the intervals (0, 1/(j+1)), j ∈ ℕ, also form a basis of 𝓝[>] 0 (`Filter.HasBasis.to_hasBasis`). In a complete lattice, the liminf along a filter with a basis is the supremum over the basic sets of the infimum over the set (`Filter.HasBasis.liminf_eq_iSup_iInf`). Therefore, for every t,
 D(t) = sup_{j∈ℕ} inf_{k∈(0,1/(j+1))} F_t(k).

2. (Left-continuity of k ↦ F_t(k); Step 5(a).) Fix t ∈ ℝ, k > 0 and real numbers q_n with q_n < k for all n and q_n → k. Then t − q_n > t − k for all n and t − q_n → t − k. So t − q_n → t − k within (t − k, ∞) (`tendsto_nhdsWithin_of_tendsto_nhds_of_eventually_within`). By hypothesis G is continuous at t − k within [t − k, ∞), equivalently within (t − k, ∞) (`continuousWithinAt_Ioi_iff_Ici`). Hence G(t − q_n) → G(t − k). Since q_n → k ≠ 0, the quotients (G(t) − G(t − q_n))/q_n converge to (G(t) − G(t − k))/k. Since ofReal is continuous, F_t(q_n) → F_t(k).

3. (Rational infimum; Step 5(b).) For every t ∈ ℝ and δ > 0,
 inf_{k∈(0,δ)} F_t(k) = inf_{q∈ℚ, q∈(0,δ)} F_t(q).
 “≤”: every rational q ∈ (0, δ) is a real number in (0, δ), so the left side is ≤ F_t(q) for each such q.
 “≥”: let I be the right side and fix k ∈ (0, δ); we show I ≤ F_t(k).
 (i) For each n ∈ ℕ, max(0, k − 1/(n+1)) < k, because k > 0 and 1/(n+1) > 0. So there is a rational q_n with max(0, k − 1/(n+1)) < q_n < k (`exists_rat_btwn`).
 (ii) Then 0 < q_n < k < δ, so q_n ∈ (0, δ) and I ≤ F_t(q_n).
 (iii) Moreover k − 1/(n+1) < q_n < k and k − 1/(n+1) → k (`tendsto_one_div_add_atTop_nhds_zero_nat`). So q_n → k by the squeeze theorem (`tendsto_of_tendsto_of_tendsto_of_le_of_le`), and by step 2, F_t(q_n) → F_t(k).
 (iv) Every F_t(q_n) is ≥ I, so the limit is ≥ I as well (`ge_of_tendsto`): I ≤ F_t(k).
 Taking the infimum over k ∈ (0, δ) gives “≥”.

4. (Countable formula; Step 5(c).) Combining steps 1 and 3 (with δ = 1/(j+1) > 0), for every t ∈ ℝ,
 D(t) = sup_{j∈ℕ} inf_{q∈ℚ} inf_{[q∈(0,1/(j+1))]} F_t(q).
 The innermost infimum is over proofs of the proposition q ∈ (0, 1/(j+1)). It equals F_t(q) if the proposition holds and ∞ otherwise.

5. (Measurability; Step 5(d).) G is nondecreasing, hence Borel measurable (`Monotone.measurable`). Fix q ∈ ℚ. The map t ↦ t − q is measurable, so t ↦ G(t − q) is measurable. Hence t ↦ (G(t) − G(t − q))/q is measurable (difference of measurable functions, division by a constant), and so is t ↦ F_t(q) (`ENNReal.measurable_ofReal`). For fixed j and q, the infimum of this function over the t-independent proposition q ∈ (0, 1/(j+1)) is measurable (`Measurable.iInf_Prop`). A countable infimum over q ∈ ℚ (`Measurable.iInf`) and a countable supremum over j ∈ ℕ (`Measurable.iSup`) of measurable [0, ∞]-valued functions are measurable. By the formula of step 4, D is Borel measurable. ∎
proof_key_steps: The intervals (0, 1/(j+1)), j ∈ ℕ, form a basis of 𝓝[>] 0, so D(t) = sup_j inf_{k∈(0,1/(j+1))} F_t(k) (Filter.HasBasis.liminf_eq_iSup_iInf).
Right-continuity of G makes k ↦ F_t(k) = ofReal((G(t) − G(t−k))/k) left-continuous at each k > 0.
The infimum over real k ∈ (0,δ) equals the infimum over rational q ∈ (0,δ): approximate k from the left by rationals q_n ∈ (max(0, k − 1/(n+1)), k) and apply ge_of_tendsto.

D(t) = sup_j inf_{q∈ℚ} inf_{[q∈(0,1/(j+1))]} F_t(q). Each t ↦ F_t(q) is measurable because G is monotone, hence measurable. So D is measurable by Measurable.iInf_Prop, Measurable.iInf and Measurable.iSup.

audit.reason: Both hypotheses are explicit and correctly used. Right-continuity gives convergence under rational approximation from the left in k; the rational-infimum equality and countable neighborhood basis yield the stated Borel measurability. The proof is complete and independent of distribution_regularity.

subproblem.title: Distribution function of ν on (a,b) is nondecreasing and right-continuous (parent Step 2(a),(d))
subproblem.statement: Let ν be a Borel measure on ℝ and a, b ∈ ℝ with ν((a,b)) < ∞. For r ∈ ℝ let G(r) := ν((a,b) ∩ (−∞, r]), taken as a real number (ENNReal.toReal; the value is finite). Then G is nondecreasing on ℝ. G is also right-continuous at every s ∈ ℝ, i.e. G(r) → G(s) as r → s within [s, ∞) (ContinuousWithinAt G (Ici s) s).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (ν : Measure ℝ) (a b : ℝ), ν (Ioo a b) ≠ ∞ → Monotone (fun r : ℝ => (ν (Ioo a b ∩ Iic r)).toReal) ∧ ∀ s : ℝ, ContinuousWithinAt (fun r : ℝ => (ν (Ioo a b ∩ Iic r)).toReal) (Ici s) s
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, Step 2(a) (G is nondecreasing) and Step 2(d) (G is right-continuous, by continuity of ν from above). Here they are stated for an arbitrary Borel measure ν on ℝ and reals a, b with ν((a,b)) < ∞. The parent applies this to its distribution function G(s) = ν((a,b) ∩ (−∞, s]) in the case Q = ν((a,b)) < ∞. The conclusion supplies the hypotheses of the sibling lemma dini_measurable.

Setting. ν is a measure on the Borel σ-algebra of ℝ, a, b ∈ ℝ and Q := ν((a,b)) < ∞. For r ∈ ℝ put A_r := (a,b) ∩ (−∞, r] and G(r) := (ν(A_r)).toReal.

1. (Finiteness.) For every r we have A_r ⊆ (a,b), hence ν(A_r) ≤ Q < ∞ (`measure_mono`, `ne_top_of_le_ne_top`). So ν(A_r) ≠ ∞ for every r.

2. (G is nondecreasing; Step 2(a).) Let r ≤ r′. If x ∈ A_r, then x ∈ (a,b) and x ≤ r ≤ r′, so x ∈ A_{r′}. Thus A_r ⊆ A_{r′} and ν(A_r) ≤ ν(A_{r′}). Since ν(A_{r′}) ≠ ∞ by step 1, toReal preserves this inequality (`ENNReal.toReal_mono`), so G(r) ≤ G(r′).

3. (Reduction to the open half-line.) Fix s ∈ ℝ. Continuity of G at s within [s, ∞) is equivalent to continuity of G at s within (s, ∞) (`continuousWithinAt_Ioi_iff_Ici`). That is, it is equivalent to G(r) → G(s) as r → s along the filter 𝓝[>] s. We prove the latter.

4. (Continuity from above.) Consider the family (A_r) for r > s.
 (i) Each A_r is a Borel set (an open interval intersected with a closed half-line), in particular ν-null-measurable.
 (ii) The family is monotone: if s < i ≤ j then A_i ⊆ A_j (step 2).
 (iii) Some member has finite measure: s + 1 > s and ν(A_{s+1}) < ∞ by step 1.
 Continuity of measures from above, for a family decreasing as r ↓ s, gives ν(A_r) → ν(⋂_{r>s} A_r) as r → s along 𝓝[>] s (`tendsto_measure_biInter_gt`; the index type ℝ is linearly ordered, order-topological and first countable).

5. (The intersection equals A_s.) Suppose x ∈ A_r for every r > s. Taking r = s + 1 gives x ∈ (a,b). Also x ≤ r for every r > s. Hence x ≤ s: otherwise any r with s < r < x would give x > r (formally `le_of_forall_gt_imp_ge_of_dense`). So x ∈ A_s. Conversely, if x ∈ A_s and r > s, then x ≤ s < r, so x ∈ A_r. Hence ⋂_{r>s} A_r = A_s, and step 4 reads: ν(A_r) → ν(A_s) as r → s along 𝓝[>] s.

6. (Passing to real values.) Since ν(A_s) ≠ ∞ (step 1), toReal is continuous at ν(A_s) (`ENNReal.tendsto_toReal`). Composing with step 5 gives G(r) = (ν(A_r)).toReal → (ν(A_s)).toReal = G(s) as r → s along 𝓝[>] s. This is continuity of G within (s, ∞) at s. By step 3 it is continuity within [s, ∞) at s.

7. (Conclusion.) By step 2, G is monotone. By step 6, for every s ∈ ℝ, G is continuous at s within [s, ∞) (ContinuousWithinAt G (Ici s) s). ∎
proof_key_steps: For A_r := (a,b) ∩ (−∞, r], ν(A_r) ≤ ν((a,b)) < ∞, so G(r) = ν(A_r).toReal is a faithful real value.
r ≤ r′ ⇒ A_r ⊆ A_{r′} ⇒ G(r) ≤ G(r′) (measure_mono, ENNReal.toReal_mono).
Right-continuity within Ici s is equivalent to continuity within Ioi s (continuousWithinAt_Ioi_iff_Ici).
Continuity from above (tendsto_measure_biInter_gt) for the decreasing Borel family A_r, r ↓ s, using ν(A_{s+1}) < ∞, gives ν(A_r) → ν(⋂_{r>s} A_r) = ν(A_s).
ENNReal.tendsto_toReal at the finite value ν(A_s) gives G(r) → G(s) as r → s+.

audit.reason: The finiteness hypothesis matches the Lean type and suffices without a < b or global finiteness of ν. The proof establishes finite values, monotonicity, the exact decreasing-family intersection, continuity from above, and passage through toReal. No sibling or parent theorem is used.
